newsitem.title: JAPAN: China to allow brokerages to open branches - report.
newsitem.headline: China to allow brokerages to open branches - report.

text.p: China plans to allow foreign securities houses to open branches, seek establishment of five joint ventures in tourism and cut tariffs across the board to 15 percent, a Japanese daily reported on Sunday.

The leading economic journal Nihon Keizai Shimbun said China's measures will be included in its so-called "Individual Action Plan" for liberalising trade and investment, to be submitted at a ministerial meeting of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum in Manila later this month.

The Nihon Keizai said China will allow foreign brokerages to open branches by 2000, increase the number of branches of foreign banks and insurance firms, and study plans to allow foreign banks to handle the Chinese currency.
China will allow the establishment of five new joint venture tourism firms, the Nihon Keizai said.
China will also reduce import tariffs, now at an average 23 percent, to 15 percent by 2000, and seek to continue reducing them beyond that year, the daily said.
China's plan forms part of APEC's overall Action Plan to open up the region's trade and investment.
The regional grouping has set up a goal of liberalising trade and investment by 2010 for industrialised economies and 2020 for developing ones.
